root_cause.text: The EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT flag was unconditionally passed to ext4_split_convert_extents() during pre-I/O extent splitting, causing the EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2 flag to be set even when the extent had not yet been written to disk, which resulted in the on-disk extent being marked as initialized while the extent status tree remained unwritten, creating a stale data exposure window if the subsequent I/O operation failed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that the problematic code path in ext4_ext_handle_unwritten_extents() was calling `ext4_split_convert_extents(handle, inode, map, path, flags | EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT, allocated)` unconditionally. The fix removes the `| EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT` addition and modifies ext4_split_convert_extents() to only set `EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2` when `EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT` is explicitly present in flags: `if (flags & EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT) split_flag |= EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2`. The CVE description confirms that when ext4_split_extent_at() fails with -ENOSPC after partial zeroing, the EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2 flag causes the entire on-disk extent to be converted to written state while the extent status tree remains partially unwritten, exposing stale data if the DIO write subsequently fails.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit INTRODUCES the fix for the vulnerability described. The root cause was that EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT was unconditionally passed to ext4_split_convert_extents(), causing EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2 to be set prematurely. The fix in this commit adds conditional logic: (1) In ext4_split_unwritten_extents() at lines 3340-3341, the EXT4_EXT_DATA_VALID2 flag is now CONDITIONALLY set only 'if (flags & EXT4_GET_BLOCKS_CONVERT)', preventing unconditional marking. (2) In ext4_convert_unwritten_extents_endio(), the function now takes a 'map' parameter and checks if the extent needs splitting before conversion (lines 3366-3377), adding race-condition protection. (3) The zeroout logic in ext4_split_extent_at() now properly handles DATA_VALID flags (lines 2980-2987) to avoid marking extents as initialized when they contain valid data. This commit fixes the vulnerability rather than introducing it.
